NEW PATIENT VISIT

64 y/o retired construction foreman here to establish. Previous PCP retired and he 'let it slide' for a while. No acute complaints today. Wants refills set up locally.

CHRONIC PROBLEMS (per pt and the med bottles he brought; old records requested):
- HTN - on lisinopril 20 and HCTZ 25 for years. Doesn't check at home.
- High cholesterol - atorvastatin 40 qhs.
- COPD - olodaterol inhaler, 2 puffs every morning. Gets winded on stairs and carrying things but says that's been the same a long time. Smoker's cough in the mornings.
- PAD - on the old problem list, he says he was told 'poor circulation' in the legs. Currently denies leg pain with walking.
- AAA - small, found on an ultrasound some years back. Followed by vascular surgery, he thinks every year or two. Doesn't remember the size. Brother has one too.
- Rheumatic fever as a boy. Was told his heart was fine afterward; no known valve problem.

PSH: diagnostic laparoscopy for belly pain around age 45 (~1998), no records, he doesn't know what they found.
Meds: lisinopril 20 daily, HCTZ 25 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, ASA 81 daily, olodaterol 5 mcg (2 inh) daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father MI at 58. Mother HTN, stroke at 72. Brother AAA.
SH: smokes 1 ppd since age 21, ~44 pk-yr. Beer 1-2 a week. Drives. Retired from construction (foreman).

ROS: neg for chest pain, syncope, edema, melena. +chronic morning cough, white phlegm.

EXAM: Gen well-appearing, smells of smoke. HEENT ok. Neck no bruit. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs diminished throughout, prolonged expiration, no wheeze today. Abd soft, nontender, I think I feel aortic pulsation midline, not tender. Ext no edema, DP/PT palpable bilaterally, feet warm. Skin ok.

A/P:
1. HTN - at goal today on lisinopril/HCTZ. BMP.
2. HLD - continue atorvastatin 40. Lipids today.
3. COPD - continue olodaterol. Discussed it is a once-daily controller, not a rescue.
4. Tobacco - 44 pk-yr, current. Talked about quitting; he's not ready to pick a date. 'Maybe after the summer.' Offered patch/meds, declined for now.
5. AAA / PAD - continue ASA. Records request to vascular surgery for last scan and plan.

REGIONAL MEDICAL CENTER - CARDIOLOGY INPATIENT SERVICE
DISCHARGE SUMMARY

Admit: 01/22/2019   Discharge: 01/25/2019

Principal diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction
Secondary: Coronary artery disease; hypertension; hyperlipidemia; COPD; peripheral arterial disease; abdominal aortic aneurysm (known, followed by vascular surgery); tobacco use.

Hospital course:
65-year-old man, current smoker, brought in early on 1/22 and found to have an acute MI with troponin elevation. He was taken urgently to the cardiac catheterization laboratory, where the culprit lesion was treated with percutaneous coronary intervention. Procedure details are in the separate catheterization report. No post-procedure complications; access site clean at discharge. Telemetry without significant arrhythmia. Started on metoprolol succinate. Ambulating in the hall without symptoms by hospital day 3. Smoking cessation counseling provided at bedside; patient declined nicotine replacement.

Discharge medications:
- Aspirin 81 mg daily (continue)
- Metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily (NEW)
- Atorvastatin 40 mg daily (continue)
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily (continue)
- Hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily (continue)
- Olodaterol 5 mcg inhaled daily (continue)

Condition at discharge: stable.
Follow-up: primary care within 2 weeks.
Instructions: no heavy lifting for 1 week, call 911 for chest pain not relieved by rest. Stop smoking.

documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY ASSOCIATES
Clinic visit 04/22/2020

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Haskins on 04/22/2020 for routine surveillance of his abdominal aortic aneurysm.

He has no new complaints. He mentions occasional mild abdominal discomfort, which he puts down to indigestion; nothing in the back, no syncope, nothing he would call pain. He is a current smoker with roughly 40 pack-years.

BP 142/88, heart rate 78.
Abdomen soft. A pulsatile mass is palpable in the periumbilical region, nontender. No abdominal bruit. Peripheral pulses intact.

Labs: hemoglobin 14.2, hematocrit 42%, fasting glucose 98.

Ultrasound that day showed an infrarenal AAA of 4.2 cm.

Impression: Infrarenal AAA, 4.2 cm, below the threshold for repair. His occasional abdominal discomfort does not sound aneurysm-related, but I have asked him to come straight to an emergency department for severe abdominal or back pain.

Plan: repeat ultrasound in 12 months. Continue aspirin and statin. I stressed that smoking is the main modifiable factor in aneurysm growth.

Thank you for allowing me to share in his care.

VASCULAR MEDICINE CONSULTATION
Date of service: 07/28/2021
Reason for referral: bilateral calf claudication

HPI: 67-year-old man with known peripheral arterial disease, coronary disease with prior MI and PCI, and an infrarenal AAA under vascular surgery surveillance, referred for calf pain with walking. He describes a consistent cramping pain in both calves after walking more than two blocks, relieved with rest. No rest pain. No tissue loss.

Medications: aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40, metoprolol succinate 50, lisinopril 20, hydrochlorothiazide 25, olodaterol.
Social: current smoker, one pack per day.

Exam: BP 142/88, HR 78. Pedal pulses diminished in both feet. Feet without ulceration.

Ankle-brachial index: 0.65 right, 0.70 left.

Aortic ultrasound in our vascular lab the same morning (vascular surgery surveillance): infrarenal AAA 4.3 cm, from 4.2 cm last year. Vascular surgery will keep him on their schedule.

Assessment: Peripheral arterial disease with bilateral intermittent claudication; ABI as above.

Recommendations:
1. Structured walking program: walk to the point of moderate calf discomfort, rest, resume, building toward 30-45 minutes most days.
2. Smoking cessation - discussed at length; this is the most important intervention for his legs and his aneurysm.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day sick visit (portal message this AM).

S: Five days of worse cough. Sputum turned thick yellow-green two days ago, more of it. More winded than his usual - stops walking across the kitchen. Wheezy at night. No fever at home, mild chills one night. No chest pain beyond soreness from coughing. No leg swelling. Using olodaterol daily since this started.
Smoking: cut down to a few cigarettes a day since he got sick.

O: T 36.7, HR 73, RR 14, BP 149/92, SpO2 89% RA.
Talking in full sentences. Lungs: diffuse expiratory wheeze and coarse rhonchi, clearing partly with cough; no focal crackles, no dullness. Prolonged expiration. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
Acute bronchitis in a man with severe COPD, purulent sputum.
- Prednisone 40 mg daily x 5 days.
- Doxycycline 100 mg BID x 7 days for the purulent sputum.
- Olodaterol daily.
- No signs of pneumonia on exam; will image if fever or not improving.
- Call or go to ED for worse breathing, confusion, chest pain.
- Sugar/BP may run up on prednisone, short course.
- Smoking: good moment to stay cut down - encouraged.
Check in by portal in a week.

documents.title: checking in
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Finished the prednisone and almost done the antibiotic. Phlegm is back to white mostly and I'm breathing like normal for me. Thanks. Lyle

documents.title: RE: checking in
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad to hear it. Finish the doxycycline. Keep the olodaterol going every day - not just when you're sick. And let me know if the phlegm turns colored again.

Smoking: back to about a pack a day since February.

O: T 37.2, HR 76, RR 14, BP 153/96, SpO2 88% RA.
Lungs: expiratory wheeze throughout, prolonged expiration, no crackles. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
Acute bronchitis on COPD, non-purulent.
- Prednisone 40 mg x 5 days.
- No antibiotic - sputum not purulent, afebrile.
- Olodaterol daily.
- Return/ED precautions reviewed.
- Two episodes in three months; he has pulm f/u in July - will make sure they know.
- Smoking: counseled, he knows.

documents.title: Vascular Surgery Surveillance Letter
documents.author: vascular surgery
documents.body:
VASCULAR SURGERY ASSOCIATES

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Haskins's aortic ultrasound on 06/17/2025 shows the infrarenal aneurysm at 4.6 cm, up from 4.4 cm two years ago. This is still below the size at which we would recommend repair, and he has no symptoms referable to it.

Given the slow growth, we will shorten his interval to a repeat ultrasound in 12 months. We again advised smoking cessation and reviewed warning symptoms.

Sincerely,
Vascular Surgery

documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
PULMONOLOGY CLINIC NOTE
Date of visit: 07/16/2025

71-year-old man with COPD and coronary disease after MI, seen for continued care of his respiratory symptoms; last here a year ago.

Breathing is worse again. Still coughing up sputum most mornings. For about two years he has been getting chest infections more often than he used to, and his PCP has treated him twice since January for bronchitis. He says he is tired of being short of breath and is open to making changes.
Smoking history about 45 pack-years per his report today.

SpO2 92% on room air.
Exam: prolonged expiratory phase with wheezing; reduced breath sounds at the bases.

Chest x-ray: hyperinflation and flattened diaphragms.
Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.65, minimally reversible with bronchodilator.

Assessment: COPD with chronic productive cough and recurrent bronchitis; continued smoking.

Plan: Discussed smoking cessation at length; he is open to it for the first time. Follow up with primary care. Return to pulmonology in one year.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV subsequent.

Outside notes reviewed:
- Pulm 7/16: CXR hyperinflation, flattened diaphragms; spirometry FEV1/FVC 0.65, minimally reversible. Smoking cessation discussed; he told them he is willing to consider changes. Return 1 yr.
- Vascular surgery 6/17: AAA 4.6 cm (4.4 in 2023), below repair threshold, rescan 12 mo.
Two bronchitis episodes this year (Jan, Apr). None since.

He brought up quitting himself today - usually I'm the one raising it. Wants to think about a date around the holidays. Talked about what's worked for others; he'd like to try on his own first.

HRA: independent, no falls, uses railings. PHQ-2 1. Alcohol 1-2/wk.
Tobacco 1 ppd, ~51 pk-yr.

Vitals: BP 150/94, HR 66, SpO2 92% RA, wt 92.7.
Exam: barrel chest, diminished BS, prolonged exp. Heart regular. Abd soft, pulsatile mass. Pedal pulses diminished. No edema.

Prevention: LDCT ordered (last 10/2024 Lung-RADS 2). FIT kit. Flu/COVID October.

A/P
1. COPD - olodaterol. Recurrent bronchitis this year.
2. HTN/HHD - 150/94. Continue lisinopril, HCTZ, metoprolol.
3. CAD/HLD - labs today.
4. AAA 4.6 cm - vascular surgery 12 mo.
5. PAD - stable.
6. Tobacco - contemplating. Revisit at December visit.

RTC 3-4 mo.
